reason: The cited evidence does not address the effect of feedstock particle size on coating thickness, deposition efficiency, or oxidation for FeCoNiCrAl. E1 studies laser cladding of different compositions, E2 examines oxidation of a different alloy under HVOF, and E3 discusses pulse energy effects in electrospark deposition, none supporting the key premises.
premises: Larger particles have lower specific surface area, reducing in-flight oxidation
Larger particles improve molten droplet formation and deposition efficiency
Larger particles produce thicker, well-adhered splats
Reduced surface oxides maintain coating integrity
Feedstock size change alone can overcome thickness shortfall without parameter adjustment
